question: Graves disease and Hashimoto thyroiditis are both autoimmune thyroid disorders, but they produce opposite functional outcomes because Graves disease involves stimulatory TSH-receptor antibodies (TSH-R Ab) whereas Hashimoto thyroiditis involves destructive antibodies (anti-TPO, anti-Tg) that cause follicular cell apoptosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The key distinction: Graves = stimulatory anti-TSHR Abs → hyperthyroidism; Hashimoto = destructive anti-TPO/anti-Tg Abs → hypothyroidism. Both are autoimmune but with fundamentally different immunological mechanisms.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In Graves disease, TSH-R Ab (thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins) continuously stimulate the TSH receptor, causing hyperthyroidism. In Hashimoto thyroiditis, anti-TPO and anti-Tg antibodies drive lymphocytic infiltration and follicular destruction, resulting in hypothyroidism.
